solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Press piles in, dreadful for evasive character

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A printing press heaping things up, behaving awfully, seems to dodge responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges PRESS PILES IN, all twelve letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipperiness is the quality of being hard to pin down or shifty, an evasive nature.

clue.text: Lots confining a pig in a wood

indicators.note: confining means the first word holds the other pieces shut inside it

parts.note: lots means many
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: Plenty of people penning a pig somewhere out in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confining' is the containment signal; 'wood' means timber, not a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a reddish-brown hardwood timber prized for furniture.

clue.text: University can set up module

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for can is written bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A university is able to arrange a course module.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses, as this is a down clue read upwards; 'can' is the noun, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a self-contained section of a course, the same thing as a module.

clue.text: Arrives in secure room at the top

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for arrives sits within the word for secure

parts.note: to get something is to secure or obtain it
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: Someone arrives inside a locked room at the top of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals containment; 'secure' is the verb meaning obtain, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A garret is an attic room just under the roof, at the very top of a house.

clue.text: Mend a dud after ordering supplementary material

indicators.note: ordering means the letters are put into a fresh arrangement, giving the answer

explanation.surface: Repair a faulty item once you've ordered some extra material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after ordering' rearranges all eight letters of the first three words; 'supplementary material' is the definition, not part of the repair job.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is an extra section added to a book or document, material supplementing the main text.

clue.text: Pleasure trip to old Sumerian city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Sumer in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A holiday excursion to the ruins of an ancient Mesopotamian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey for enjoyment visiting several places, a pleasure trip.

clue.text: Pick up king in play to take knight

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's play
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A chess move: in the game the king advances to capture a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' here is a stage play, not a game of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or language is to learn it, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Difficult and tiring with right pair in Australia

indicators.note: in says the right and pair pieces go within the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A demanding, exhausting trip as two travellers explore Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals containment of the right-plus-pair pieces within the country's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Arduous describes a task needing great effort, both hard and exhausting.

clue.text: The Spanish family initially left by artist in pose for his picture?

indicators.note: in says the run of pieces before it is placed inside the word for pose

parts.note: to sit for a painter is to pose
el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: initially takes only the opening letter of the word family

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A Spanish family's patriarch, abandoned by an artist sitting for his own portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals containment; 'by' just links. The whole clue also describes an artist posing for a picture of himself, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: When an artist paints himself, the resulting picture of his own face is a self-portrait.

clue.text: Conspirator left trapped by Voldemort's enemy

indicators.note: trapped by means the letter for left is held inside the name of the wizard

parts.note: Harry Potter is Lord Voldemort's foe in the J.K. Rowling books

explanation.surface: A schemer who quit the Dark Lord's side gets caught by Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' puts L inside POTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter devises a secret plan with others, which is what a conspirator does.

clue.text: Record name in traditional stories from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, read from the east means right to left, so the result is read backwards
in says the abbreviation for name goes inside the word for traditional stories

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories and beliefs

explanation.surface: Collecting a name found in folk tales from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside LORE to give LORNE, and 'from the east' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to enter their name on an official list, to record them.

clue.text: Detachment of troops mostly came back abnormally thin

indicators.note: back says the combined letters before it are read in reverse order
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a detail is a small group of soldiers given a special duty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of a military unit returned looking dreadfully gaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DETAIL to DETAI; 'back' reverses DETAI plus CAME, giving EMAC then IATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated describes someone wasted away by hunger or illness, far thinner than normal.

clue.text: Flawed Member of Parliament involved in current broadcast

indicators.note: involved in means the politician's abbreviation is set inside the other letters

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
aired means broadcast

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician caught up in a news item that went out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' signals containment; 'current' is electrical, not topical.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means weakened or damaged, so something with a defect is flawed.

clue.text: Pressure from retired dandy

indicators.note: retired suggests going back, so the joined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent

explanation.surface: A well-dressed gent, now retired, is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses P plus OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a man overly concerned with fashionable clothes, another word for a dandy.

clue.text: One who accepts what happens with obese top celebrities?

parts.note: fat means obese
the A-list are the most famous celebrities

explanation.surface: A resigned person who is also overweight, among the most famous stars?
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes events are predetermined and so resigns himself to whatever comes.

clue.text: Climber starting off in vertiginous Yosemite

indicators.note: starting off takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A rock climber begins up a dizzying route in Yosemite National Park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' looks like a mountaineer, fitting Yosemite, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is an evergreen plant that climbs walls and trees.

clue.text: Variable is a mere part in working out

indicators.note: working out suggests the letters are processed and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: In a sum, a variable is just one small part of the calculation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' rearranges A MERE PART.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths and science a parameter is a quantity that can vary, a variable.

clue.text: Apple user's confused time

indicators.note: confused means the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A computer user's muddled about the time on their Apple device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges USERS to RUSSE, then T is added. 'Apple' is the fruit, not the tech company.
explanation.definitionFit: A russet is a variety of eating apple with rough brownish skin.

clue.text: Lennon music regularly banished boredom

indicators.note: regularly banished means every other letter is removed, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: John Lennon's songs reliably chased away the tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly banished' drops the odd letters of LENNON MUSIC, leaving the second, fourth and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan word for listless weariness, a feeling of boredom.

clue.text: Nobody is working in north-east

indicators.note: in says the word for working sits inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: No one is employed in the north-east of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals containment; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: None means not one person, so it stands for nobody.

clue.text: Student upset choral society's leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of society
upset means the letters are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: A student upset the head of the choral society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the word choral, and 'society's leader' supplies the initial S.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or a pupil holding a scholarship, a student.

clue.text: Composer of The Planets turning out large Mass

indicators.note: turning out means the letter for large is ejected from the composer's name

parts.note: Gustav Holst composed the orchestral suite The Planets

explanation.surface: A composer producing a large-scale Mass setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' removes L from HOLST. 'Mass' is a big number, not the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great crowd or number of things, a mass of them.

clue.text: Because Jeremy's heart is honest and true

parts.note: since can mean because

indicators.note: the heart of a name is its central letters, here the middle two of Jeremy

explanation.surface: Since Jeremy has a good heart, he is honest and trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s heart' takes the central two letters of a six-letter name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere describes someone genuine and without deceit, truthful in feeling.

clue.text: Rice dish gives us hiccups to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eating a certain Japanese dish gives us a bout of hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice topped or rolled with raw fish.
